Yes. PR #2 (`automation/callisto-0.15.0`) rewrites `Formula/callisto.rb` in place, replacing every 0.14.2 URL and SHA with 0.15.0. The tap holds exactly one version per tool: the latest. The updater also refuses downgrades, so older versions can't be installed from the tap.

Homebrew's convention for this is versioned formulae, such as `Formula/callisto@0.14.rb` with `keg_only :versioned_formula`. Two details:
- Homebrew keys versioned formulae on the minor line (`@0.14`), not the patch (`@0.14.2`). Keeping 0.14.x would mean following 0.14 patch releases.
- The updater would need a step to snapshot the outgoing formula to `callisto@<old minor>.rb` (with the class renamed to `CallistoAT014`) when a new minor or major lands. A patch bump would update the existing file in place.

I'd keep only the previous minor line for each tool, not every release. That keeps CI and maintenance bounded, and it still covers the usual need of staying on the old line while you migrate. Archives for every release stay on GitHub regardless.

Do you want me to implement that in `scripts/update_formula.py`, with tests and a README/CONTRIBUTING note? Or would you rather have a different retention policy, such as every minor or the last N?
We use the gh cli for github

Understood. The PR lookup above already used `gh`, and I'll keep using it for anything on GitHub. In this sandbox `gh` can't verify TLS through the proxy, so GitHub calls need to run outside the sandbox. You can allow that with `/sandbox` if you'd rather not approve each call.

My question from before is still open: do you want me to add versioned formulae (keeping the previous minor line) to the updater?
How do we do that? How come we missed this the first time? I asked to follow homebrew best practices. What else did we miss?
I'll audit the repo against Homebrew's tap conventions before answering.

name: Update formula

on:
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [tool_released]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tool:
        description: Formula to update
        required: true
        type: string
      tag:
        description: Published release tag; leave empty to check the latest stable release
        required: false
        type: string
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 8 * * *'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  select:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.repository == 'orin-dx/homebrew-tap'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      tools: ${{ steps.select.outputs.tools }}
      tag: ${{ steps.select.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: select
        env:
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          INPUT_TOOL: ${{ inputs.tool }}
          INPUT_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
          RELEASE_TOOL: ${{ github.event.client_payload.tool }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event.client_payload.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$EVENT" in
            schedule)
              tools=$(python3 scripts/update_formula.py --list-tools)
              echo "tools=$tools" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo 'tag=' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            workflow_dispatch)
              python3 scripts/update_formula.py --validate-tool "$INPUT_TOOL"
              if [[ -n "$INPUT_TAG" && ! "$INPUT_TAG" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._@/+\-]{0,127}$ ]]; then
                echo 'Invalid release tag' >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "tools=[\"${INPUT_TOOL}\"]" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "tag=${INPUT_TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            repository_dispatch)
              python3 scripts/update_formula.py --validate-tool "$RELEASE_TOOL"
              if [[ ! "$RELEASE_TAG" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._@/+\-]{0,127}$ ]]; then
                echo 'Invalid release tag' >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "tools=[\"${RELEASE_TOOL}\"]" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "tag=${RELEASE_TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            *) exit 1 ;;
          esac

  update:
    needs: select
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        tool: ${{ fromJSON(needs.select.outputs.tools) }}
    concurrency:
      group: formula-${{ matrix.tool }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Verify release and update formula
        id: formula
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TOOL: ${{ matrix.tool }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.select.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ -n "$RELEASE_TAG" ]]; then
            version=$(python3 scripts/update_formula.py --tool "$TOOL" --tag "$RELEASE_TAG")
          else
            version=$(python3 scripts/update_formula.py --tool "$TOOL" --latest)
          fi
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if git diff --quiet -- "Formula/${TOOL}.rb"; then
            echo 'changed=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'changed=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      - name: Create tap-scoped GitHub App token
        if: steps.formula.outputs.changed == 'true'
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          owner: orin-dx
          repositories: homebrew-tap
          permission-contents: write
          permission-pull-requests: write
      - name: Open update pull request
        if: steps.formula.outputs.changed == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          TOOL: ${{ matrix.tool }}
          RELEASE_VERSION: ${{ steps.formula.outputs.version }}
          APP_SLUG: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.app-slug }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          branch="automation/${TOOL}-${RELEASE_VERSION}"
          if [[ "$(gh pr list --repo orin-dx/homebrew-tap --head "$branch" --state open --json number --jq 'length')" != 0 ]]; then
            echo "An update pull request is already open for $TOOL $RELEASE_VERSION"

          git config user.email "${bot_id}+${APP_SLUG}[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git switch -c "$branch"
          git add "Formula/${TOOL}.rb"
          git commit -m "chore: update ${TOOL} to ${RELEASE_VERSION}"
          gh auth setup-git
          git push --set-upstream origin "$branch"
          printf 'Updates the %s formula to version %s.\n\nThe tap independently fetched every supported archive, verified its published digest and contents, then recorded its SHA-256 in the formula. CI audits, installs, and tests on macOS and Linux.\n' "$TOOL" "$RELEASE_VERSION" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr-body.md"

1. **Snapshot on a minor or major bump.** Before overwriting `callisto.rb`, the updater copies it to `Formula/callisto@0.14.rb`. That copy gets the class renamed to `CallistoAT014` and `keg_only :versioned_formula` added. Patch bumps just edit the main formula.

Oxlint and oxfmt avoid our problem because their formulae have a single `url` and `sha256`. That's the shape the native bumper handles. I fetched both from homebrew-core.

- **`oxlint`** builds from source. It uses the GitHub source tarball (`oxlint_v1.90.0.tar.gz`) with `depends_on "rust" => :build` and `cargo install`. It has a plain `livecheck` block (`url :stable` plus a regex on the `oxlint_v` tag prefix). It ships bottles, and homebrew-core's tooling bumps it. I couldn't confirm which mechanism, because the autobump list URL I tried returned 404.
- **`oxfmt`** is an npm package. It uses one URL (`registry.npmjs.org/oxfmt/-/oxfmt-0.74.0.tgz`), `depends_on "node"`, and `npm install` with `std_npm_args`. npm resolves the platform-specific binary at install time, so there's no per-platform block.

Our two formulae are the other kind. They download prebuilt per-platform binaries and need four `url`/`sha256` pairs, which is what the bumper can't rewrite. Homebrew core doesn't accept that shape, so there's no standard bumping flow for it.

If we want fully native tooling, we could change what the formulae do:
- **Callisto** is Rust. It could build from a source tarball like `oxlint`, with one URL, one `livecheck`, and a plain `brew bump`. The cost is compile time for users unless we publish bottles. The tap's `publish.yml` and `brew pr-pull` flow supports bottles, but it's more setup.
- **Caliper** could follow the `oxfmt` pattern if `caliper-docgen`'s npm package pulls in the right platform binary through optional dependencies. I haven't checked that. The cost is a `node` dependency, which would undercut Caliper being a fast standalone CLI.

So the options are to keep prebuilt binaries and a small custom rewrite, or switch to source builds and `node`-based installs for fully native bumping. I'd keep the binaries, because Callisto is a CLI people install to avoid toolchains. The source-build path is worth considering for Callisto only if you're willing to run bottles.

Which direction do you want?
I like the idea of building, that's what a lot of homebrew libraries do right?

Yes. Homebrew core requires formulae to build from source, so that's the mainstream convention. Prebuilt-binary formulae like ours are the exception, which is why the tooling doesn't bump them well.

The catch is for taps. A source-build formula compiles on each user's machine unless the tap publishes bottles (prebuilt binaries Homebrew serves). Bottles need the `tap-new` pipeline: `brew test-bot` builds them, and `publish.yml` with `brew pr-pull` uploads them, typically to GitHub Packages. Without bottles, `brew install callisto` pulls in Rust as a build dependency and compiles. That's slow and heavy.

Whether this works depends on the upstream repos, so I'll check what they actually build.

- **Naming.** Versioned formulae are named by line, not patch. Pre-1.0 the minor is the breaking boundary, so `@0.14`. After 1.0 it would be `@1`. Users on `callisto@0.14` get 0.14.x patches only, and the livecheck regex is pinned to `^callisto@(0\.14\.\d+)$`. They can't pin to 0.14.2 exactly.
- **What gets simpler.** The bumper updates every formula the same way, versioned ones included, so there's no custom code for patch releases on old lines. The downgrade guard goes away too. The four `explicitVersion` overrides become at most one top-level `version`. We might not need even that if Homebrew can parse the `callisto%400.15.0` tag from the URL, which I haven't verified.
- **What stays manual.** When a new minor ships, someone snapshots the outgoing formula to `callisto@<old minor>.rb`, renames the class, adds `keg_only :versioned_formula`, and pins its livecheck. Old lines should be deleted once they're unsupported. A small script or `brew extract` can do the snapshot step. Homebrew doesn't automate it.
- **Bottles.** Each versioned formula has its own bottles, built once per release of that line. Old lines cost CI time only when a patch lands.
- **Reproducibility.** Source builds keep any old release buildable from its tag, and `brew install --HEAD` becomes possible with a `head` stanza.

What happens if we do brew install without from-source?

Right now it's identical to `--build-from-source`. The formula has no `bottle do` block, so Homebrew has nothing to pour and compiles from source, pulling in `rust` and `llvm` as build dependencies. The `--build-from-source` flag only matters once bottles exist.

- Skip build dependencies, so no Rust, LLVM or Z3 is installed.
- Fall back to a source build if no bottle matches the user's platform (for example a newer macOS than CI built for), or for `--HEAD`.

Bottles come from the `tap-new` pipeline:
1. `brew test-bot` builds one bottle per runner on each PR.
2. After approval, `brew pr-pull` uploads them to the tap's bottle host (GitHub Packages by default) and adds the `bottle do` block, with `root_url` and per-platform checksums, to the formula.

The bottle matrix only covers the platforms we build on, so we'd keep the four runners we test on now. That's about the same coverage as the prebuilt archives we ship today.

We want this to be easy for users

- Any platform without a bottle falls back to compiling, which pulled in 2.4 GB (`rust`, `llvm`, `z3`) in my test.
- Bottles lag behind releases until `brew pr-pull` publishes them.
- A broken bottle pipeline degrades every install, not just updates.

1	# How tap updates work
2	
3	The tap follows published CLI releases. It does not decide when Callisto or Caliper publishes, and a release workflow does not write a formula directly.
4	
5	## The path from release to PR
6	
7	1. A trusted release workflow sends `tool_released` with a tool name and tag. The tap also checks for new stable versions every day, so a missed event does not strand a release.
8	2. [`scripts/update_formula.py`](../scripts/update_formula.py) reads the tool's committed manifest. It fetches publisher metadata and every platform archive, verifies the published digest, checks archive contents and executable mode, then writes four SHA-256 values to the formula.
9	3. The tap creates a short-lived GitHub App token scoped to this repository and opens a branch and PR. It does not overwrite an existing update branch or downgrade a formula.
10	4. **Required tap checks** runs updater tests, then audits, installs, and exercises the changed formula on macOS ARM/Intel and Linux ARM/x86-64. Shared updater changes and a weekly run check every formula. A maintainer reviews and approves the PR, including any new runtime library or minimum OS requirements.
11	
12	The event cannot choose a download URL or checksum. Both come from the manifest on `main` and the publisher's versioned release. The SHA-256 in a merged formula is the digest Homebrew checks on every later install.
13	
14	## One-time GitHub setup
15	
16	### Create the App
17	
18	Create an organization-owned GitHub App called something like `orin-dx-homebrew-updater`. Disable its webhook. Give it only **Contents: read and write** and **Pull requests: read and write**, then install it on **only `orin-dx/homebrew-tap`**. The notification needs Contents write for GitHub's `repository_dispatch` endpoint; the tap also needs Pull requests write to open the review PR.
19	
20	Generate one private key and record the App's client ID. Keep the PEM out of Git and terminal output. Store them as an organization Actions variable and secret, each visible only to `homebrew-tap`, `callisto`, and `caliper`:
21	
22	```sh
23	gh variable set TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID --org orin-dx --repos homebrew-tap,callisto,caliper
24	gh secret set TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY --org orin-dx --repos homebrew-tap,callisto,caliper < path/to/downloaded-key.pem
25	```
26	
27	The variable command prompts for the client ID. The secret command reads the PEM from stdin; delete the downloaded file after storing it. Add Firkin to the selected repositories only when its release notifier exists. The App never needs access to the source repositories themselves.
28	
29	### Protect `main`
30	
31	After the first tap commit lands, add a repository ruleset for `main`: require a PR, one approval, dismiss stale approvals after new pushes, and require **Required tap checks**. Do not give the App a bypass. The sole maintainer can use an admin PR-only bypass for human-authored maintenance; bot formula PRs still need that maintainer's approval. Leave automatic merge off.
32	
33	The tap workflow's default `GITHUB_TOKEN` is read-only. Its App token is minted only after all archives pass verification and only for `homebrew-tap`. Source repositories use the same shared [notification action](https://github.com/orin-dx/actions/tree/main/notify-homebrew-tap) after a successful release, with their receipt proving a CLI was published. They have no formula-editing code.
34	
35	## Run or recover an update
36	
37	Run **Update formula** in the tap's Actions tab or use the CLI:
38	
39	```sh
40	gh workflow run update-formula.yml -R orin-dx/homebrew-tap -f tool=caliper
41	gh workflow run update-formula.yml -R orin-dx/homebrew-tap -f tool=callisto -f tag=callisto@0.14.2
42	```
43	
44	Without App credentials, verification still runs but the workflow cannot open a changed-formula PR. You can run the updater locally and submit a human PR instead. If an update branch already exists, inspect its PR and branch before retrying; the workflow refuses to force-push over it. To rotate the App key, replace `TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` in the selected organization secret and revoke the old key in the App's settings.

Yes, much simpler. Here is the per-release flow now:

1. The upstream repo tags a release, optionally sending the existing `tool_released` dispatch. The daily schedule catches it anyway.
2. `brew bump` (the `autobump.yml` workflow) sees the new tag via `livecheck` and opens a PR changing one `url` and one `sha256`.
3. `brew test-bot` builds, tests, and bottles it on all four runners.
4. A maintainer approves the PR and runs the publish workflow (`brew pr-pull`), which uploads the bottles and merges.

That removes `update_formula.py`, the manifests, the digest and contents verification, and four-way checksum editing. Adding a tool is now one formula file. Two things stay manual: snapshotting `callisto@0.14.rb` when a new minor ships, and the publish click.

**What the source repos need**

All three (callisto, caliper, monokl) are public Rust repos:
- Tag stable releases as `X.Y.Z` with a consistent prefix, so the tap's `livecheck` regex matches.
- Commit `Cargo.lock`, keep the build free of git metadata (`git describe` and the like), and keep `rust-version` current with Homebrew's Rust. Callisto and Caliper already meet this.
- Keep a `completions` subcommand and a CLI crate that builds on its own. The formulae use `crates/callisto-cli` and `crates/cli`.
- Optionally keep calling `notify-homebrew-tap` after a release. It's still accepted, and the payload is ignored. Without it, a new release can wait up to a day.
- The prebuilt archives and npm platform packages are no longer needed by the tap, so keep them only for other install paths.

**Per repo**
- **Callisto:** nothing required.
- **Caliper:** nothing required. Its tags (`npm/caliper-docgen@x`) are matched by a regex that ignores the sibling `caliper-docgen-napi` tags. The tap was at 0.5.0 while 0.7.0 exists upstream, so the old updater was lagging. I don't know why, and the new formula starts at 0.7.0.
- **Monokl:** it's an AST-aware code search CLI in Rust, but it has no GitHub releases yet. It needs a first tagged release and a stable tag format. Then adding it is one `Formula/monokl.rb` with a `livecheck` and a test. I haven't looked at its crate layout or CLI.

**Tap-side setup I can't do from here**
- The `main` ruleset requires **Required tap checks**, which no longer exists. It needs to require the `brew test-bot` jobs instead.
- Bottles go to GitHub Packages by default, and the generated `publish.yml` may need package write access. That's unverified until the first real `pr-pull`.

I'll keep going on the cleanup of the old updater and docs.

# How tap updates work

The tap follows tagged releases. It does not decide when Callisto or Caliper publishes, and a release workflow does not write a formula directly. The three workflows are the ones `brew tap-new` generates, with a few additions noted below.

## The path from release to bottles

1. **Detect.** The **brew bump** workflow (`autobump.yml`) runs daily and on a `tool_released` event from a tool's repository. It runs `brew bump --open-pr`, which asks each formula's `livecheck` block for the newest stable tag and opens a PR that changes the source `url` and `sha256`. A missed event is caught by the next daily run.
2. **Test.** **brew test-bot** (`tests.yml`) styles and audits the tap, then builds, tests, and bottles each changed formula on macOS ARM and Intel and Linux ARM and x86-64. Bottles are uploaded as workflow artifacts.
3. **Review.** A maintainer reads the PR, including any new build or runtime requirements, and approves it once the test-bot jobs pass.
4. **Publish.** The maintainer runs **brew pr-pull** (`publish.yml`) with the PR number. It uploads the bottles, adds the `bottle do` block to the formula, attests build provenance, and pushes to `main`.

The release event cannot choose a download URL or checksum. The URL comes from the formula and the tag from `livecheck`; `brew bump` computes the checksum itself.

## One-time GitHub setup

### Create the App

Pull requests opened with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger other workflows, so the bump workflow uses a short-lived GitHub App token instead. Create an organization-owned GitHub App called something like `orin-dx-homebrew-updater`. Disable its webhook. Give it only **Contents: read and write** and **Pull requests: read and write**, then install it on **only `orin-dx/homebrew-tap`**. The notification needs Contents write for GitHub's `repository_dispatch` endpoint.

Generate one private key and record the App's client ID. Keep the PEM out of Git and terminal output. Store them as an organization Actions variable and secret, each visible only to `homebrew-tap`, `callisto`, and `caliper`:

```sh
gh variable set TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID --org orin-dx --repos homebrew-tap,callisto,caliper
gh secret set TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY --org orin-dx --repos homebrew-tap,callisto,caliper < path/to/downloaded-key.pem
```

The variable command prompts for the client ID. The secret command reads the PEM from stdin; delete the downloaded file after storing it. The App never needs access to the source repositories themselves.

### Protect `main`

Add a repository ruleset for `main`: require a PR, one approval, dismiss stale approvals after new pushes, and require the **brew test-bot** jobs (one per platform). Do not give the App a bypass. The sole maintainer can use an admin PR-only bypass for human-authored maintenance. Leave automatic merge off. The publish workflow pushes bottle commits to `main`, so its actor needs to be allowed by the ruleset.

### Bottle storage

`brew pr-pull` uploads bottles to GitHub Packages for this repository by default. If the first publish run fails on package permissions, grant the workflow package write access or use a release-asset `root_url`. This has not been exercised yet.

## Run or recover an update

Run **brew bump** from the tap's Actions tab, or use the CLI:

```sh
gh workflow run autobump.yml -R orin-dx/homebrew-tap
gh workflow run publish.yml -R orin-dx/homebrew-tap -f pull_request=<number>
```

If a bump PR already exists for a version, `brew bump` skips it. To rotate the App key, replace `TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` in the selected organization secret and revoke the old key in the App's settings.

See [Contributing](../CONTRIBUTING.md) for formula changes and [Security](../SECURITY.md) for private reporting.

name: Notify Homebrew tap
description: Send a versioned release event to an Orin DX Homebrew tap with a tap-scoped GitHub App token.

inputs:
  client-id:
    description: GitHub App client ID. The App must be installed on the target tap.
    required: true
  private-key:
    description: GitHub App private key, passed from an Actions secret.
    required: true
  tap-repository:
    description: GitHub owner/repository of the tap.
    required: true
  tool:
    description: Tool name configured in the tap, such as callisto or caliper.
    required: true
  release-tag:
    description: Published upstream release tag.
    required: true

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Validate dispatch target
      id: target
      shell: bash
      env:
        TAP_REPOSITORY: ${{ inputs.tap-repository }}
        TOOL: ${{ inputs.tool }}
        RELEASE_TAG: ${{ inputs.release-tag }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        if [[ ! "$TAP_REPOSITORY" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]]; then
          echo 'Expected tap-repository as owner/repository' >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        if [[ ! "$TOOL" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$ ]]; then
          echo 'Invalid tap tool name' >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        if [[ ! "$RELEASE_TAG" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._@+/-]{0,127}$ ]]; then
          echo 'Invalid release tag' >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "owner=${TAP_REPOSITORY%%/*}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        echo "repository=${TAP_REPOSITORY#*/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    - name: Create tap-scoped token
      id: app-token
      uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3
      with:
        client-id: ${{ inputs.client-id }}
        private-key: ${{ inputs.private-key }}
        owner: ${{ steps.target.outputs.owner }}
        repositories: ${{ steps.target.outputs.repository }}
        permission-contents: write
    - name: Dispatch release
      shell: bash
      env:
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        TAP_REPOSITORY: ${{ inputs.tap-repository }}
        TOOL: ${{ inputs.tool }}
        RELEASE_TAG: ${{ inputs.release-tag }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        gh api "repos/${TAP_REPOSITORY}/dispatches" -f event_type=tool_released -f "client_payload[tool]=${TOOL}" -f "client_payload[tag]=${RELEASE_TAG}"
